---
title: "3A. Sample mapping (track A: insects)"
format:
  html:
    toc: false
---

*Explore the spatial distribution of samples and their associated habitat types across Sweden.*

### Inspect contextual data

Core sample-level metadata is available in `merged$events`, an ordinary data frame with one row per sample:

```r
events <- merged$events
colnames(events)
```

---

### Extract temporal variables

Latitude and longitude can be used directly, whereas `eventDate` requires some preparation because dates in these two datasets are stored as `start/end` intervals. We therefore first extract the start of each interval before calculating month and day of year.

A few records only contain a year and no exact date. These cannot be assigned a month or day of year, so they are left as `NA`. We exclude these records below when filtering the samples used in the analyses.

```r
event_start <- lubridate::parse_date_time(
  sub("/.*", "", events$eventDate),
  orders = c("ymd_HMSz", "ymd_HMS", "ymd"),
  quiet = TRUE
)
events$month <- lubridate::month(event_start)
events$yday  <- lubridate::yday(event_start)
events$date  <- as.Date(event_start)
```

---

### Extract habitat type

The `env_local_scale` column contains habitat type classifications based on the [Environment Ontology](https://sites.google.com/site/environmentontology/){target="_blank"} (ENVO). We first inspect the unique values:

```r
unique(events$env_local_scale)
```

For plotting, we create short labels and assign a colour to each habitat:

```r
habitat_map <- c(
  "forested area [ENVO:00000111]"    = "forest",
  "area of cropland [ENVO:01000892]" = "cropland",
  "wetland area [ENVO:00000043]"     = "wetland",
  "grassland area [ENVO:00000106]"   = "grassland",
  "urban biome [ENVO:01000249]"      = "urban",
  "alpine biome [ENVO:01001835]"     = "alpine"
)
events$habitat <- unname(habitat_map[events$env_local_scale])

habitat_cols <- c(
  "forest"    = "#2d6a4f",
  "cropland"  = "#d4a017",
  "wetland"   = "#4895ef",
  "grassland" = "#95d5b2",
  "urban"     = "#adb5bd",
  "alpine"    = "#9b5de5"
)
```

---

### Filter samples

Samples with very few total reads are excluded, as their community composition is unreliable, and so are the handful with an incomplete `eventDate`. We get the sequencing depth of each sample with a query on the long table:

```r
depth <- merged$counts |>
  summarise(depth = sum(organismQuantity, na.rm = TRUE), .by = eventID) |>
  as.data.frame()

events <- merge(events, depth, by = "eventID")
summary(events$depth)  # inspect before picking a threshold

samples <- events[events$depth >= 100000 & !is.na(events$yday), ]
nrow(samples)
```

`100000` is a reasonable depth threshold here. Check the `summary()` output above and adjust it if it excludes far more or fewer samples than expected for your dataset.

---

### Pair the two extraction methods

The two datasets differ in size (homogenate: ~860 samples; lysate: ~4,550), and they do not cover the same places and dates. To compare the extraction methods fairly, we keep only samples from site and date combinations that occur in both, so that differences between the methods are not mixed up with differences between sites and seasons:

```r
samples$method <- sub(":.*", "", samples$eventID)
samples$site_date <- paste(samples$locationID, samples$date)

shared <- Reduce(intersect, split(samples$site_date, samples$method))
samples <- samples[samples$site_date %in% shared, ]
table(samples$method)
```

From here on, `samples` is the fixed set of samples used throughout the rest of the tutorial. Each site and date occurs twice, once per extraction method. Remember this if you interpret habitat or season, since the two samples of a pair are not independent.

---

### Map samples

We define a function that plots monthly maps of the study area, showing where and when samples were collected, with point colour indicating habitat type:

```r
plot_monthly_maps <- function() {
  newmap <- rworldmap::getMap(resolution = "low")
  par(mfrow = c(4, 4), mar = c(2, 2, 3, 1), xpd = TRUE)

  for (m in 1:12) {
    in_month <- samples[samples$month == m, ]
    plot(newmap, xlim = c(10, 25), ylim = c(55, 70), asp = 1, main = month.abb[m])
    if (nrow(in_month) > 0) {
      points(in_month$decimalLongitude, in_month$decimalLatitude, pch = 21,
             col = "black", bg = habitat_cols[in_month$habitat], cex = 1.5)
    }
  }

  plot.new()
  legend("left", bty = "n", legend = names(habitat_cols),
         pt.bg = habitat_cols, pch = 21, pt.cex = 1.6, cex = 1.1,
         title = "Habitat")
}

plot_monthly_maps()
```

This figure has several panels and can look cramped on a laptop screen. Click **Zoom** above the Plots pane for a larger view. Points also overlap since paired samples share a location, and nearby sites (~10–15 km apart) can coincide at this scale, so it looks sparser than the actual sample count.
